source_text: Ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτό ἐστιν ἰδεῖν τὸ τῆς θαλάσσης ὕδωρ παρὰ τῶν ναυτιλλομένων ἑψόμενον· οἳ τοὺς ἀτμοὺς σπόγγοις ὑποδεχόμενοι, τὴν χρείαν μετρίως ἐν ταῖς ἀνάγκαις παραμυθοῦνται. Καλὴ δὲ καὶ ἄλλως παρὰ Θεῷ, ὅτι περισφίγγει τὰς νήσους, ὁμοῦ μὲν κόσμον αὐταῖς, ὁμοῦ δὲ καὶ ἀσφάλειαν παρεχομένη δι' ἑαυτῆς· ἔπειτα καὶ ὅτι τὰς πλεῖστον ἀλλήλων διεστώσας ἠπείρους συνάπτει δι' ἑαυτῆς, ἀκώλυτον τοῖς ναυτιλλομένοις τὴν ἐπιμιξίαν παρεχομένη· δι' ὧν καὶ ἱστορίας τῶν ἀγνοουμένων χαρίζεται, καὶ πλούτου πρόξενος ἐμπόροις γίνεται, καὶ τὰς τοῦ βίου χρείας ἐπανορθοῦται ῥᾳδίως, ἐξαγωγὴν μὲν τῶν περιττῶν τοῖς εὐθηνουμένοις παρεχομένη, ἐπανόρθωσιν δὲ τοῦ λείποντος χαριζομένη τοῖς ἐνδεέσι. Καὶ πόθεν ἐμοὶ ὅλον ἰδεῖν μετὰ ἀκριβείας τῆς θαλάσσης τὸ κάλλος, ὅσον τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ποιήσαντος κατεφάνη; Εἰ δὲ θάλασσα καλὴ καὶ ἐπαινετὴ τῷ Θεῷ, πῶς οὐχὶ καλλίων ἐκκλησίας τοιαύτης σύλλογος, ἐν ᾗ συμμιγὴς ἦχος, οἷόν τινος κύματος ἠϊόνι προσφερομένου, ἀνδρῶν καὶ γυναικῶν καὶ νηπίων, κατὰ τὰς πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ἡμῶν δεήσεις, ἐκπέμπεται. Γαλήνη δὲ βαθεῖα ἀσάλευτον αὐτὴν διασώζει, τῶν πνευμάτων τῆς πονηρίας ταράξαι αὐτὴν τοῖς αἱρετικοῖς λόγοις μὴ δυνηθέντων. Γένοισθε οὖν ἄξιοι τῆς ἀποδοχῆς τοῦ Κυρίου, τὴν εὐταξίαν ταύτην ἐπὶ τὸ εὐπρεπέστατον διασώσαντες, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν. ΟΜΙΛΙΑ εʹ. Περὶ βλαστήσεως γῆσ 5.1 Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Θεός· βλαστησάτω ἡ γῆ βοτάνην χόρτου, σπεῖρον σπέρμα κατὰ γένος, καὶ ξύλον κάρπιμον ποιοῦν καρπὸν κατὰ γένος, οὗ τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ. Ἀκολούθως μετὰ τὸ ἀναπαύσασθαι τὴν γῆν ἀποσκευασαμένην τὸ βάρος τοῦ ὕδατος, τὸ πρόσταγμα αὐτῇ γέγονε βλαστῆσαι πρῶτον βοτάνην, ἔπειτα ξύλον· ὅπερ ἔτι καὶ νῦν ὁρῶμεν γινόμενον. Ἡ γὰρ τότε φωνὴ, καὶ τὸ πρῶτον ἐκεῖνο πρόσ ταγμα, οἷον νόμος τις ἐγένετο φύσεως, καὶ ἐναπέμεινε τῇ γῇ, τὴν τοῦ γεννᾶν αὐτῇ καὶ καρποφορεῖν δύναμιν εἰς τὸ ἑξῆς παρεχόμενος. Βλαστησάτω ἡ γῆ. Πρῶτόν ἐστιν ἐν τῇ γενέσει τῶν φυομένων ἡ βλάστησις· ἔπειτα, ὅταν προκύψῃ μικρὸν τὰ βλαστήματα, βοτάνη γίνεται· εἶτ' ἐπειδὰν αὐξηθῇ, χόρτος ἐστὶ, κατὰ μικρὸν διαρθρουμένων τῶν φυομένων, καὶ μέχρι τῆς ἐπὶ τὸ σπέρμα τελειώσεως προϊόντων. Τὸ γὰρ χλοερὸν καὶ ποάζον παραπλήσιόν ἐστιν ἁπάντων. Βλαστησάτω ἡ γῆ βοτάνην χόρτου. Καθ' ἑαυτὴν ἡ γῆ προφερέτω τὴν βλάστησιν, οὐδεμιᾶς συνεργείας ἑτέρωθεν δεομένη. Ἐπειδή τινες οἴονται τὸν ἥλιον αἴτιον εἶναι τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς φυομένων, τῇ ὁλκῇ τοῦ θερμοῦ πρὸς τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν τὴν ἐκ τοῦ βάθους δύναμιν ἐπισπώμενον, διὰ τοῦτο πρεσβυτέρα τοῦ ἡλίου ἡ περὶ γῆν διακόσμησις· ἵνα καὶ τοῦ προσκυνεῖν τὸν ἥλιον, ὡς αὐτὸν τὴν αἰτίαν τῆς ζωῆς παρεχόμενον, οἱ πεπλανημένοι παύσωνται. Ἐὰν ἄρα πεισθῶσιν, ὅτι πρὸ τῆς ἐκείνου γενέσεως τὰ περὶ τὴν γῆν πάντα διακεκόσμητο, καὶ τοῦ ἀμέτρου περὶ αὐτὸν θαύματος καθυφῶσιν, ἐνθυμηθέντες ὅτι χόρτου καὶ βοτάνης νεώτερός ἐστι κατὰ τὴν γένεσιν. Ἆρα οὖν τοῖς μὲν βοσκήμασιν ἡ τροφὴ προαπετέθη, τὸ δὲ ἡμέτερον οὐδεμιᾶς ἐφάνη προνοίας ἄξιον; Ἀλλὰ μάλιστα μὲν ὁ βουσὶ καὶ ἵπποις τὸν χιλὸν προαποθέμενος, σοὶ τὸν πλοῦτον καὶ τὴν ἀπόλαυσιν παρα σκευάζει.
thought_title: The sea's beauty and the church's calm
orientation: Basil is concluding his praise of the sea's usefulness and beauty, then turns to praise the gathered church and introduces the fifth homily on vegetation.
pass_a_gloss: But also it is possible to see the very water of the sea being boiled by sailors; who, receiving the vapors with sponges, moderately relieve their need in their necessities. And it is beautiful also in another way before God, because it encircles the islands, providing at once adornment for them and at once also safety through itself; then also because it joins together through itself the continents that stand farthest apart from one another, providing unhindered intercourse for sailors; through which things it also grants knowledge of things unknown, and becomes a provider of wealth for merchants, and easily sets right the needs of life, providing export of surplus goods for those who abound, and granting correction of what is lacking to those in need. And from where is it possible for me to see with accuracy the whole beauty of the sea, as much as appeared to the eye of the Maker? But if the sea is beautiful and praiseworthy to God, how is not more beautiful the assembly of such a church, in which a mingled sound, like that of some wave approaching a shore, of men and women and infants, according to our prayers to God, is sent up. And a deep calm preserves it unshaken, since the spirits of wickedness were not able to trouble it with heretical words. May you therefore become worthy of the acceptance of the Lord, preserving this good order to the most fitting degree, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be the glory and the power unto the ages of ages. Amen. HOMILY 5. On the sprouting of the earth 5.1 And God said: let the earth sprout herb of grass, seed-bearing according to kind, and fruit tree producing fruit according to kind, whose seed is in it. Fittingly, after the earth rested, having put off the weight of the water, the command came to it to sprout first herb, then tree; which thing even now we see happening. For the voice then, and that first command, became like a certain law of nature, and remained in the earth, providing to it for the future the power of generating and bearing fruit. Let the earth sprout. First in the generation of growing things is the sprouting; then, when the sprouts come forth a little, herb comes to be; then when it grows, it is grass, the growing things being articulated little by little, and proceeding as far as the completion unto seed. For the green and grassy state is similar in all. Let the earth sprout herb of grass. By itself let the earth bring forth the sprouting, needing no cooperation from elsewhere. Since some think the sun to be the cause of the things growing from the earth, drawing up by the attraction of heat the power from the depth to the surface, for this reason the ordering of the earth is older than the sun; so that also those who have gone astray may cease from worshiping the sun, as if it provided the cause of life. If then they are persuaded that before the generation of that one all things concerning the earth had been ordered, they will also lower their excessive wonder about it, having considered that it is younger than grass and herb according to generation. Was then food set out beforehand for the cattle, but our own appeared worthy of no forethought? But most especially the one who stored up fodder beforehand for oxen and horses is preparing wealth and enjoyment for you.

choices.why: σπεῖρον is a neuter singular participle agreeing with βοτάνην, describing the herb as bearing seed, not an action of sowing
μάλιστα μὲν is emphatic, not contrastive correction; it intensifies the point rather than correcting it
The term means mutual mixing or interchange, here commercial and social exchange between distant lands
The verb means to lay aside or remove a burden, fitting the earth's release from the weight of water
The verb means to be divided into distinct parts or joints, describing the gradual differentiation of plant growth

pass_b_english: You can also see the water of the sea being boiled by sailors: they catch the vapors with sponges and so relieve their need in emergencies, sufficiently. It is beautiful in another way in God's sight as well, because it encircles the islands, providing them at once with adornment and with safety through itself. Then too, because it joins together the continents that stand farthest apart from one another, offering sailors unhindered intercourse; through this it grants knowledge of things unknown, becomes a source of wealth for merchants, and easily supplies the needs of life, providing export for the surplus of those who abound and granting relief for the lack of those in need. And how could I see with precision the whole beauty of the sea, as much as appeared to the eye of its Maker? If the sea is beautiful and praiseworthy to God, how much more beautiful is the assembly of such a church, in which a mingled sound—like a wave breaking on the shore—is sent up from men and women and infants in their prayers to our God. A deep calm preserves it unshaken, since the spirits of wickedness have not been able to trouble it with heretical words. May you then become worthy of the Lord's approval, preserving this good order in the most fitting way, in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.
HOMILY 5: On the Sprouting of the Earth

And God said, "Let the earth sprout the herb of grass, seed-bearing according to kind, and the fruit tree producing fruit according to kind, whose seed is in it" (Genesis 1:11). It follows that after the earth had rested, having put off the weight of the water, the command came to it to sprout first herb, then tree—which we still see happening now. For that voice then, and that first command, became like a law of nature and remained in the earth, granting it the power to generate and bear fruit for the time to come. "Let the earth sprout." First in the generation of growing things is the sprouting; then, when the sprouts come up a little, herb appears; then, when it has grown, it is grass, as the growing things are gradually articulated and advance to the completion of the seed. For the green and grassy state is similar in all of them. "Let the earth sprout the herb of grass." Let the earth bring forth the sprouting by itself, needing no cooperation from any other source. Since some people think the sun is the cause of the things that grow from the earth, drawing up the power from the depths to the surface by the attraction of heat, for this reason the ordering of the earth is older than the sun—so that those who have gone astray may stop worshiping the sun as though it provided the cause of life. If they are persuaded that everything concerning the earth was ordered before the sun's creation, they will also let go of their excessive wonder at it, considering that it is younger than grass and herb in its origin. Was food then laid out beforehand for the cattle, while our own provision appeared worthy of no forethought? But surely the one who stored up fodder for cattle and horses beforehand is above all preparing wealth and enjoyment for you.

problems.source_quote: ὁ βουσὶ καὶ ἵπποις τὸν χιλὸν προαποθέμενος, σοὶ τὸν πλοῦτον καὶ τὴν ἀπόλαυσιν παρασκευάζει
problems.why: Missing 'most especially' force of μάλιστα; and the logic is concessive/corrective—'But surely the one who... is [all the more] preparing... for you'; 'most especially' was omitted in rendering.
problems.fix: But surely the one who stored up fodder for cattle and horses beforehand is all the more preparing wealth and enjoyment for you
problems.ruling: μάλιστα ('most especially') in source is omitted from English rendering; shifts emphasis of argument's conclusion.

edits.old: But most especially, the one who stored up fodder for oxen and horses beforehand is preparing wealth and enjoyment for you.
edits.new: But surely the one who stored up fodder for cattle and horses beforehand is all the more preparing wealth and enjoyment for you.

fixed: The English omitted the force of μάλιστα and the concessive/corrective logic. The source reads 'Ἀλλὰ μάλιστα μὲν ὁ βουσὶ καὶ ἵπποις τὸν χιλὸν προαποθέμενος, σοὶ τὸν πλοῦτον καὶ τὴν ἀπόλαυσιν παρασκευάζει.' The new rendering 'But surely... is all the more preparing...' captures the corrective force and the emphasis.

problems.why: βοτάνην χόρτου is 'herb of grass' or 'grass-herb', but the English reverses the natural order; it's 'herb [that becomes] grass'.
problems.fix: herb of grass, seed-bearing according to kind

problems.why: μάλιστα μὲν...σοὶ is 'especially for you' or 'above all for you', not 'all the more'; it's a climax, not a comparative.

problems.ruling: μάλιστα μὲν...σοὶ = 'especially/above all for you'; 'all the more' wrongly implies comparison rather than climactic emphasis.
